title: Product Counsel
description: ABOUT US Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia. We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do. Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace. WHAT YOU’LL DO We're hiring a Product Counsel to be a core member of Sierra's growing legal team. This role will report to our Associate General Counsel, Product and Privacy, as part of our growing product legal function. We are looking for someone who has deep expertise in product counseling for AI or other emerging technologies. You will be a legal partner for Sierra’s product and engineering teams, and help shape how our products go to market responsibly, ensuring privacy, compliance, and risk considerations are embedded throughout the product lifecycle. You will thrive in dynamic environments, enjoy tackling challenges beyond your comfort zone, and be excited to contribute across the business. In return, we'll provide the support and opportunities you need to grow and excel as a lawyer. You'll be part of a legal team that is highly respected within the company — committed to excellence, collaboration, and making a meaningful impact. Product - End-to-end responsibility for product legal support: counsel Product and Engineering teams from concept through launch across Sierra's agent platform and new products. - Work closely with Engineering teams to integrate compliance and privacy-by-design principles and AI transparency measures into product development. - Advise the customer-facing Agent Development teams on legal requirements of product features, including consumer protection, telecommunications (e.g., voice and messaging), and industry-specific requirements for regulated customers. - Develop scalable product review processes, launch checklists, and self-serve guidance that let product teams move quickly. Regulatory (with focus on AI) - Advise on emerging AI-specific regulations and their applicability to Sierra's products. - Partner with the privacy team to implement AI governance policies and frameworks to ensure responsible AI deployment. - Monitor legal developments affecting AI products, advising product leadership on risks, trends, and design implications. WHAT YOU’LL BRING - 4+ years of legal experience, with a combination of large international law firm and in-house experience at a tech company. - Experience advising product and engineering teams on new product development, ideally involving AI/ML, communications, or platform products. - Working knowledge of the legal domains that touch product development, including privacy (e.g., GDPR, CCPA), AI regulatory frameworks (e.g., EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework), consumer protection, and IP. - Ability to partner with technical teams to understand all aspects of Sierra's product offering. - Strong analytical skills and the ability to balance legal risks and business objectives in a fast-moving environment. - Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to partner with both legal and non-legal stakeholders. - A strong work ethic with an eye for detail. You will strive for perfection, and expect that of others. - Be a team player first and foremost. Sierra is a unique place to work, with a strong sense of togetherness, and the legal team is no exception. You will look out for your colleagues, be accustomed to sharing and helping the team succeed. EVEN BETTER… - Experience with voice/telephony products and related regulatory regimes (e.g., TCPA, state call recording laws). - Experience counseling on products sold into regulated industries (healthcare, financial services). - Familiarity with machine learning models and their associated risks. - Previous experience developing trust and safety or responsible AI programs. - Startup experience and comfort with rapid iteration and ambiguity. title: Research Counsel
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a member of the Research Legal team, you'll advise on legal topics across the full lifecycle of building and studying frontier AI models: data acquisition and use, training pipelines, model evaluation and launch, and alignment, interpretability, model welfare, societal impacts, and beneficial deployments research, as well as Responsible Scaling Policy work on biological risk. You'll be a subject matter expert on copyright, privacy, data use, and AI regulation (including the EU AI Act, U.S. state laws, and emerging global rules), and will work directly with researchers on questions that often have no settled answer. The ideal candidate will have navigated complex legal questions at the intersection of machine learning, data, and academic research in a fast-moving technical environment, with the judgment to work at the cutting edge of AI development while effectively solving issues, enabling innovation, and calibrating risk. This is a uniquely positioned role touching many different facets of AI, presenting the opportunity to be a leader in AI legal thought.  Key responsibilities Advise research and data teams on data sourcing, licensing, partnerships, and use, and help shape Anthropic's data acquisition and use strategy as laws and markets evolve Help coordinate regulatory readiness and model launches, review model documentation and system cards, respond to regulatory inquiries, and advise on legal questions for pre-release and internal models Support the Responsible Scaling Policy as applied to biological and chemical risk, including capability evaluations, tiered access for biosecurity researchers, and dual-use research questions Counsel the Societal Impacts, Economic, Alignment, Interpretability, Model Welfare, and Beneficial Deployments teams on research design, data collection and sharing, external collaborations, program launches, and publication review Monitor global AI, privacy, copyright, and export-control developments and translate them into practical internal guidance and policy, working closely with Product, Policy, and other legal stakeholders Engage with academics, regulators, industry groups, and civil society to help develop norms and best practices for responsible AI development and data governance Minimum qualifications Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based (California or New York preferred) Practical, creative problem-solving: the ability to apply legal requirements to fast-changing, deeply technical work, with an understanding that the goal is to enable responsible research and product development in a risk-calibrated environment Exceptional communication and analytical skills, technical fluency, and the ability to navigate ambiguous and uncharted legal territory, turning complex technical and legal analysis into advice people can act on Familiarity and comfort advising on the EU AI Act, U.S. legislation and AI frameworks, GDPR/CCPA, and comparable regimes globally, sometimes where no AI-specific legislation exists Interest in thinking deeply about the impact of AI on society and how to make humanity's transition to the AI age as beneficial as possible Sound judgment about when to be flexible and when to hold a line; comfort making high-stakes calls in unsettled areas and outside your core expertise; and a low-ego, collaborative approach, doing the work needed rather than delegating it or being territorial Preferred qualifications At least 8 years of legal experience advising technology companies on copyright, privacy, data, AI regulation, and related product and policy issues, ideally including time in-house and work on AI/ML products or services Experience engaging directly with regulators or standards bodies Working technical literacy: enough familiarity with how models are trained, evaluated, and deployed to ask researchers and engineers the right questions and spot the legal issues in a technical design An academic or publishing background, or experience with copyright, open-source, and data licensing Experience with biosecurity, dual-use research, export controls, or safety frameworks such as Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy Experience advising on academic or industry research, including publications, external collaborations, data sharing, or human-subjects and consent questions, ideally in AI or an adjacent technical field Role-specific policy: We prefer candidates who can work from our San Francisco or New York office at least 3 days a week, but may consider other locations for the right candidate. title: Temp Legal Counsel (Product Legal)
description: Our Purpose At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here. About Us SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters. Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity. What Are We Looking For? We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes. As a Temporary Attorney, you will be tasked with providing legal support for product initiatives while also helping our commercial team with escalations and other matters. You will support a growing business and work closely with cross-functional partners as an effective individual contributor and collaborative team player, acting as a trusted advisor to business and legal leadership across both product compliance and commercial GTM operations. Please note this is a 6 month contract position, starting December 1st.  What Will You Do? Primary responsibilities include: Product & AI Counseling: Provide pragmatic legal advice on product initiatives, emerging AI features, and related regulatory topics. Commercial Support: Partner with GTM teams to handle commercial escalations and address customer inquiries. Third-Party Risk Review: Evaluate AI tools and vendor assessments to support internal legal and risk standards. Cross-Functional & Incident Response: Support legal priorities across compliance, and special projects as needs evolve What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring? I deal candidates will have: In-house experience at a technology company, with transactional and product counseling experience. Proven track record supporting commercial legal. Familiarity with key legal and regulatory frameworks relevant to AI products and systems, as well as general privacy regulations in the SaaS space (e.g., GDPR, CPRA, EU AI Act). Well-grounded knowledge of intellectual property and SaaS commercial contracts law. Ability to organize, prioritize, and manage a high-volume workload in a fast-paced environment with excellent written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated sound and practical business judgment in counseling clients and navigating complex negotiations and high-pressure situations. Highly responsive with a service-focused approach to supporting commercial, product, engineering teams. Bias and drive for action, fast learning, and proactive problem solving. Preferred: Experience or familiarity with incident response protocols, and relevant notification requirements. Preferred: Experience evaluating third-party software, AI tools, and vendor security/privacy assessments. Preferred: Demonstrated interest or experience in cybersecurity and SaaS GTM legal operations. Preferred: Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP). This U.S. role has a base pay range that will vary based on the location of the candidate. For some locations, a different pay range may apply.  If so, this range will be provided to you during the recruiting process. You can also reach out to the recruiter with any questions. Base Salary Range $156,000 — $215,000 USD SentinelOne is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. SentinelOne participates in the E-Verify Program for all U.S. based roles.

title: Director, Litigation and Regulatory
description: About Sezzle: With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! About the Role:  Sezzle is a publicly traded consumer finance company (Nasdaq: SEZL) building purchase-now-pay-later products for consumers who are underserved by traditional credit, and we are pursuing a de novo national bank charter. That combination puts us in front of regulators, plaintiffs' counsel, and state enforcement authorities more often than a company our size would normally be, and we handle almost all of it in-house.  This role is for a lawyer who wants to own that work rather than route it. You will run litigation and pre-litigation disputes, manage regulatory inquiries and investigations from federal and state authorities, and serve as the legal owner of our privacy and data protection framework. You will have real autonomy on day one, direct access to the executive team, and the budget discipline of a lean function that brings in outside counsel deliberately rather than reflexively. What You'll Do: Litigation and disputes Manage consumer litigation, class actions, arbitrations, and commercial disputes from intake through resolution, including case strategy, discovery, and settlement posture. Direct outside counsel where we use it: scope, budget, staffing, and strategy. You set the plan; they execute it. Own litigation holds, ESI protocols, custodian identification, and the discovery process end to end. Manage the small-claims and arbitration pipeline, and build the process improvements that keep volume from becoming a drag. Identify the patterns behind repeat disputes and take them back to product, operations, and collections so the underlying problem gets fixed. Regulatory inquiries and investigations Manage civil investigative demands, examination requests, subpoenas, and informal inquiries from the CFPB, FTC, state attorneys general, and state financial regulators. Run productions: scope negotiation, data collection, privilege review, and delivery, working with engineering, data, and compliance. Draft response letters, white papers, and advocacy submissions, and participate directly in regulator meetings. Track the enforcement and supervisory landscape across BNPL, UDAAP, credit reporting, debt collection, and consumer disclosure, and translate it into concrete guidance for the business. Support supervisory readiness as we build toward bank charter approval and the examination posture that follows. Privacy and data protection Serve as legal owner of the privacy framework: policies, notices, records of processing, data mapping, and retention. Advise on state comprehensive privacy laws, GLBA, FCRA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, and the pixel and session-replay wiretap theories that continue to generate demand letters and class actions. Review vendor and partner data flows, negotiate data protection terms, and handle escalated consumer privacy rights requests. Partner with the Chief Compliance and Privacy Officer on incident response and on the operational privacy program. AI and how the function scales Use AI to multiply your own throughput across research, document review, discovery, production, drafting, and regulatory tracking, and keep pushing what that stack can do. Build durable tooling, not one-off prompts: skills, workflows, templates, and automations that outlive the matter they were built for and that the rest of the team can run. Champion responsible AI adoption across the company. Legal is a builder here, not a brake. You will help business teams find ways to use these tools well and help set the guardrails that make that possible. Advise on AI governance as a legal matter: model use, vendor diligence, data handling, disclosure, and the emerging regulatory picture. Advisory and cross-functional Counsel product, marketing, engineering, and collections on live questions with practical answers, not memos that end in “it depends.” Build the playbooks, templates, and internal training that let the function scale without adding headcount. What We Look For: Bachelor's degree from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing in at least one US jurisdiction. You will need to satisfy in-house counsel

title: Senior Product Manager (Data Governance Platform)
description: We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time. Product Manager AI adoption across the organization is accelerating, and existing governance processes can add cycle time and rely heavily on manual review. We are building an AI Governance Engineering capability to modernize governance through automation—shifting from approval-heavy workflows to registration-driven workflows with built-in controls, and continuous observability. As a product manager in AI Governance team, you will be responsible for managing the vision, roadmap and requirements for the engineering team delivering governance-as-code roadmap: platform-agnostic SDKs, APIs, and automated controls that help teams move faster while ensuring responsible AI guardrails are consistently enforced. This role is a combination of product manager and product owner roles where you will need to operate at both 10000 ft as well as ground level providing granular requirements that team can execute on. Responsibilities Define product strategy, capabilities, and roadmaps for the governance as code team of engineers. Define Agent to agent workflows Research industry practices in this domain and choose best bath forward taking an agile approach to development Establish shared vision across the company by building consensus on priorities. Building influential relationships with business partners, stakeholders, and peer group to drive outcomes. Meet with internal stakeholders, exhibitors, and buyers to gather requirements, understand customer needs, and define product features Conducting thorough business case and value analysis to prioritize scope and approach of solutions Work with other Product Mangers and Product Owners to determine and manage cross-team dependencies. Define and analyze metrics that inform the success of our platform and related products. Following human centered thinking to design, develop and facilitate working sessions to compile business needs and user feedback. Review epics and refine user stories with the Engineering to support the development process Coordinate with the UI/UX team to define short and long-term goals and produce actionable artifacts. Maintain accurate and actionable user stories throughout the development life cycle in the new era of agentic development Verify stories are completely based on acceptance criteria. Learn and master industry knowledge and product management skills by staying curious in nature and continuously learning. Participate in the incident management process as required to support overall issue resolution. Identifying, managing, and mitigating risks at program and product level and communicate to appropriate stakeholders. Participate in Agile ceremonies such as stand ups, sprint demos, and retrospectives Identify and build relationships with key users to establish a regular cadence of feedback gathering. Exceptional soft skills, including the ability to articulate to both technical and business audiences. Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills and demonstrated experience in using tools such as Excel, Visio, Miro, PowerPoint. Minimum Qualifications: 7+ years of experience as a Product Manager working in a large, matrixed organization with many internal partners. 5+ years of experience working in an Agile methodology, using Agile productivity tools, leading incremental software releases. 5+ years of experience working on data and analytics-based platform capabilities, services, or products. 3+ years of experience working with UI/UX teams to develop wireframes and working prototypes based on end user feedback and human centered design. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with Responsible AI concepts such as fairness, transparency, explainability, and auditability. Background working in regulated or high-trust technology environments. Ability to translate governance or risk requirements into scalable solutions Education Undergraduate degree required Graduate degree preferred Preference given to candidates with degrees and credentials in agile, product management, data and analytics related fields What Success Looks Like AI intake processes are simpler, faster, and largely automated. Engineering teams have reusable SDKs and templates that make responsible AI the default. Validation of controls shifts from self-reporting to automated checks and evidence. Centralized observability provides real-time insight into AI usage, performance, and risk. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. Reporting to the Senior Director, Commercial Legal, based in the UK, you will lead a team of four to five lawyers while remaining a key individual contributor.   This highly visible, hands-on leadership role combines team oversight with direct involvement in complex software transactions.
